label: Discrete Groups
notes: Open by setting the chapter's program. Discrete groups acting on the model geometries determine the closed manifolds the geometries can support. The deck follows printed pages 209 through 288: small generators, Euclidean and crystallographic groups, elliptic manifolds, thick-thin decomposition and Teichmuller coordinates, and fibered geometries Nil and Sol.

label: Margulis-Style Near-Identity
notes: Present the chapter's first structural rule. A discrete subgroup of a Lie group cannot keep producing new elements arbitrarily close to the identity unless it is forced into a controlled nilpotent pattern. The notebook uses two near-identity unipotent matrices; their commutator is even closer to the identity, which is the finite-matrix shadow of the Margulis lemma.

label: Crystallographic
notes: Cover Euclidean crystallographic groups. Each such group fits in a short exact sequence: lattice of translations, then finite point group. The graph encodes this exact sequence. The 3D ledger compares three familiar lattice families that appear in the crystallographic classification: cubic, hexagonal, and tetragonal frames.

label: Elliptic Three-Manifolds
notes: Move to elliptic three-manifolds: quotients of S^3 by finite groups acting freely. The classification splits into lens-space cases driven by cyclic groups, and binary polyhedral families driven by extensions of icosahedral, octahedral, and tetrahedral symmetry. The slide is a route map, not a copied list.

label: Thick-Thin Decomposition
notes: Introduce the thick-thin decomposition for hyperbolic manifolds. Points with small injectivity radius form thin regions, typically cusps or tubes around short geodesics. The complement is the thick part. The chapter uses this to sort geometric behavior locally before any global classification.

label: Teichmuller
notes: Sketch Teichmuller space. It records hyperbolic structures on a surface up to isotopy, with coordinates given by lengths of curves and Fenchel-Nielsen twists. The picture combines a synthetic injectivity-radius lab with the moduli interpretation: small injectivity radius signals approach to the boundary of Teichmuller space.

label: Fibered Geometries
notes: Cover the fibered model geometries. Nil and Sol arise as extensions of one-dimensional Lie groups; closed Nil-manifolds and Sol-manifolds appear in the geometrization picture as quotients of these nilpotent and solvable Lie groups. The chapter records their exact-sequence structure as classification data.

label: Applied Lab
notes: Walk through the lab. Take two near-identity matrices, compute the commutator and its distance to the identity, and confirm that iterated commutators shrink in the operator norm. The lab is the Margulis-lemma analogue in finite dimensions and prepares students to read the abstract statement in the source text.

label: Recap
notes: Close with the chapter takeaways. Discreteness forces near-identity behavior to be nilpotent. Euclidean crystallographic groups are lattice plus finite point group. Elliptic three-manifolds are sorted by finite quotients of the sphere. Thick-thin sorts hyperbolic manifolds locally. Teichmuller space parametrizes hyperbolic surface structures. Nil and Sol round out the fibered classification.
